Subject: High error rate & latency since 09/13 evening - immediate help needed

Hey Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xxs and very high p99 tail latency on your inference endpoints beginning ~2026-09-13 19:30 EDT. Our monitoring shows ~12% 5xx rate on /v1/infer and 4x normal p99. Screenshots attached, and I've attached a pcap of a failed session.

This is affecting two pilot customers and our demo environment. We suspect something changed on our side or the peering paths around the time the cloud provider did maintenance in our region. Can you triage urgently and let us know next steps?

Impacted: us-east-1 endpoints (model: small-chat-3), sample request IDs: req-21534, req-21591

Thanks,
- Ops (Sentinel)

Thanks for the heads-up and the pcap — I'm escalating now.

Quick questions while we dig in:
- Are the errors consistent across all Sentinel accounts or only the demo/pilot tenants?
- Any NAT/proxy in your VPC egress that could be rate-limiting or injecting timeouts?

Vanessa and Marcus — looping you in to triage network path and proxy behavior.

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, ops@sentinelhealth.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-13T21:34:00-04:00
Subject: Initial triage: signs of asymmetric path and proxy 503s

Thanks for the pcap — I pulled out the following:
- Multiple TCP retransmits and RSTs in short windows, followed by application-level 503s from a corporate proxy IP (35.190.12.81) that sits in front of their egress.
- Upstream RTTs to our LB are normal when traffic takes the direct path, but the sessions that go via the proxy show a 2.3s extra hop and repeated connection resets.
- No evidence of model-serving queue spikes on our side for the sample request IDs. CPU/GPU look normal.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Ask Sentinel to route our traffic via their dedicated egress NAT (bypass the corporate proxy) — fastest if they can change a route.
2) We can temporarily accept traffic on our alternate peering IP in us-east-1 that avoids the suspect AS; I can coordinate an IP failover in ~30m.

I've attached a short trace summary (trace_summary_20260914.txt). Marcus, can you open an INF ticket for a rapid IP failover and prep the canary route policy?

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Network Reliability

Please escalate to anyone required on your side. We need:
- ETA for stabilization (minutes/hours)
- Confirmation of root cause (if you have it)
- Any temporary workarounds we can apply from our network side immediately

Regards,

jonathan.price@sentinelhealth.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-14T08:21:00-04:00
Subject: Plan: canary route + cloud peering ticket (INF-5421)

Plan:
- In 25 minutes we'll provision an alternate public egress IP for Sentinel traffic in us-east-1 and add a canary routing rule that prefers the direct path (avoids the proxy AS). Expected cutover time: ~30 minutes.
- Opened INF-5421 for cloud provider peering flap investigation and requested expedited support.
- If the canary reduces 5xxs, we'll move remaining traffic over during a controlled window.

I'll execute the canary and post status here. Marcus, can you coordinate the failover? Vanessa, please keep monitoring the p99.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber | Site Reliability

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T08:40:00-04:00
Subject: Exec update (internal): Sentinel outage impact & recommended customer credit

Quick internal update for leadership:
- Impact: Sentinel production and demo environments experienced ~10–12% 5xx rate and p99 increased ~4x between 2026-09-13 19:30 EDT and 2026-09-14 08:00 EDT for specific peering paths.
- Root cause (prelim): Traffic from Sentinel is transiting a corporate proxy/NAT that intermittently drops and resets connections (AS path asymmetry). Not a runtime GPU overload on our side.
- Mitigation: Canary route provisioned at 08:25 EDT; initial traffic diverted off the suspect path. 5xxs dropped to <1% for canary traffic.
- Ask: Approval to offer Sentinel a one-week service credit and to prioritize the INF ticket with the cloud provider. Also recommend a follow-up post-incident review with Sentinel's network team to harden peering/e2e routing.

I'll wait for confirmation from Jonas on canary metrics and then propose the customer communication.

— Soojin

From: ops@sentinelhealth.com
